title: two-pointer and sliding-window techniques
concepts: Two pointers track positions whose movement is justified by an ordering property or a maintained invariant.
Opposite-direction pointers can eliminate candidate pairs when sorted order or a symmetric objective proves which endpoint to move.
Same-direction read and write pointers support stable in-place filtering and compaction.
A sliding window is a contiguous range whose state is updated as its boundaries move.
Fixed-size windows add the entering value and remove the leaving value once per step.
Variable-size windows expand and contract while maintaining a validity condition; monotone validity is needed for a linear scan.
Frequency maps or counters maintain membership and multiplicity information for strings and arrays.
The at-most-K technique can derive exactly-K counts by subtracting the at-most-(K-1) count when the counting identity applies.
Sorting may enable a two-pointer scan but changes original order and adds preprocessing cost.
Negative numbers can break the monotone sum condition needed by common variable-size sum windows.
